papers.title: FAN: Foresight Action Normalization for Continual Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.title_zh: FAN: Foresight Action Normalization for Continual Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models pre-trained on large-sca
papers.cover_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models pre-trained on large-sca
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models pre-trained on large-scale, closed datasets have demonstrated remarkable success across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. However, their long-term real-world deployment necessitates continuously acquiring new skills while retaining previously learned capabilities. While pioneering works have explored continual VLA adaptation using techniques such as experience replay and reinforcement fine-tuning, they overlook a foundational mechanism: action normalization, which determines the underlying coordinate system in which policies perceive and execute physical actions. To bridge this gap, we systematically evaluate five normalization strategies across four real-world task streams covering single-arm and bimanual manipulation. Our analysis reveals that existing protocols induce severe failure modes due to inter-task coordinate drift, limited motion coverage, or train-test coordinate mismatches. Motivated by these insights, we formulate three core design principles: consistency, coverage, and causality (3C), and introduce foresight action normalization (FAN). FAN estimates normalization statistics once from a small, task-independent calibration set prior to continual learning and freezes them throughout adaptation. Across all evaluated streams, FAN achieves the highest performance and demonstrates consistent robustness, providing insightful guidance for building stable action representations in achieving effective lifelong VLA adaptation.

papers.title: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation
papers.title_zh: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation
papers.tldr_zh: Generative world models offer controllable and repeatable cl
papers.cover_zh: Generative world models offer controllable and repeatable cl
papers.abstract_zh: Generative world models offer controllable and repeatable closed-loop simulation for end-to-end and vision-language-action driving policies, but production deployment exposes three unresolved requirements: faithfully reproducing a mixed fisheye-pinhole rig at native resolutions; reconciling causal, per-timestep interaction with long-horizon stability and low latency; and preserving scene identity when a location is revisited. We present ZYT-World, a single architecture that natively generates four fisheye views with field of view > 180° and three pinhole views. Projection-specific Plucker adapters encode camera geometry, ego-motion adaptive layer normalization provides global motion control, and a lightweight pixel-aligned layout conditions traffic participants and signals through instance-level boxes, headings and colors. Heterogeneous training combines full-rig geometric coverage with high-resolution detail. Teacher forcing, causal consistency distillation, self-rollout distribution matching distillation, and RigCritic transform a 40-step bidirectional teacher into a one-step, per-latent streaming generator, with RigCritic evaluating the seven-view rig jointly. A 19M-parameter variational autoencoder decoder (TinyVAE), W8A8 quantization, and our inference engine reduce decoding, backbone, and incremental-execution costs, respectively. Finally, cross-trajectory pairs derived from real captures train a plug-in implicit-memory module that preserves place-specific evidence. On the internal multi-view test set, the one-step model retains more than 90% of the teacher's PSNR and SSIM, while FID, FVD, and LPIPS stay within 11% of the teacher. Under the generator-only timing in Figure 2, it is 107.7 times faster than the 40-step bidirectional teacher. TinyVAE decodes 59.8 times faster than Wan. 30s rollouts and cross-trajectory revisits show the intended long-horizon and memory behavior.

papers.title: SkelWAM: A Skeleton-Guided World-Action Model for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
papers.title_zh: SkelWAM：用于零样本跨具身操作的骨架引导世界-动作模型
papers.tldr_zh: SkelWAM用骨架几何表示实现零样本跨具身操作，成功率超基线36.2个百分点。
papers.cover_zh: 零样本跨具身操作｜SkelWAM用骨架几何让机器人直接上手
papers.abstract_zh: 跨机器人具身复用操作经验对于扩展机器人学习、减少重复的任务特定数据采集至关重要。然而，具身变化会改变视觉外观、动作维度和语义，以及能够实现相同工具位姿的全身构型。我们提出SkelWAM，一种骨架引导的世界-动作模型，通过单一显式几何表示将感知与控制耦合，用于单源跨具身操作。手臂中心线几何、工具中心点（TCP）位姿和平行夹爪命令构成共享的25维状态。相同的定义构成了规范第三人称和腕部观测以及未来全身动作目标的基础。在预测性视觉监督下训练，视频-动作混合Transformer预测规范骨架动作块，具身特定的约束解码器将其转换为关节或连续体机器人控制。该公式不需要一对一的关节对应，也不使用目标任务的演示或目标策略更新。我们引入了LIBERO-Cross10，一个仅源域的跨具身迁移基准，涵盖四个形态组的十个任务和十个目标具身。在该基准上，Franka训练的SkelWAM在1000个回合中达到43.3%的成功率，超过最佳评估基线36.2个百分点。我们进一步将JAKA mini2训练的策略部署到Feagine A03连续体机器人上，用于三个桌面操作任务，展示了该方法在真实世界跨具身操作中的潜力。项目页面：http://www.liukepku.com/skelwam/index.html

papers.title: LIMBO: Learning and Internalizing Model-Free Barrier Objectives for Agile and Safe Whole-Body Control
papers.title_zh: LIMBO：学习并内化无模型障碍目标，实现敏捷安全的全身控制
papers.tldr_zh: LIMBO 学习并内化安全证书，实现无在线过滤的敏捷全身控制。
papers.cover_zh: 不用在线安全过滤｜这个框架让机器人学会后仰 limbo 绝技
papers.abstract_zh: 安全全身控制需要在高维非线性动力学下协调避碰与平衡，这使得安全证书难以设计且难以在不同行为间复用。我们提出 LIMBO，一个用于合成状态-动作控制障碍函数并将其安全结构蒸馏到任务策略中的框架。LIMBO 从黑盒转移和基于状态的失败规范中学习安全证书，该规范作用于冻结基础控制器周围的残差动作，使得 Q-CBF 合成在全控制维度上可行，同时将证书置于任务策略的控制空间中。在合成过程中，学习到的安全值驱动风险引导采样，在可恢复性估计边界附近进行探索；在任务学习中，它作为教师提供动作级安全反馈，产生鲁棒的任务策略，并减轻部署时对在线安全过滤器的需求。我们在一个 29 自由度的类人机器人上演示了 LIMBO，执行躲避球和低障碍物下运动任务。除了将学习到的 Q-CBF 扩展到全身控制之外，我们还表明风险引导边界采样提供了一种有理论依据的方式来探索可恢复性的边缘。在相同的安全规范下，其他条件不变，改变采样集中度会产生从蹲伏到新颖的后仰 limbo 策略。在两种设置中，学习到的策略无需在线安全过滤即可迁移到硬件，表明学习到的安全合成可扩展到敏捷全身控制。

papers.title: SeeQ: Training Generalist Value Functions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.title_zh: SeeQ：训练通用价值函数用于长时程机器人操作
papers.tldr_zh: SeeQ通过子任务级Q函数缩短信用分配范围，提升长时程机器人操作策略。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人长任务总翻车？SeeQ让价值函数学会拆解子任务
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管通用机器人策略取得了快速进展，但在复杂的长时程任务中仍然表现脆弱，这些任务包含多个阶段，或者需要在同一底层阶段反复尝试和思考才能成功。Q值函数可以通过对候选动作排序或指导策略改进来提升这些策略，但从稀疏的任务级奖励中学习会带来长信用分配范围、困难的贝尔曼备份以及广泛的数据覆盖需求。我们提出了SeeQ（子任务诱导Q函数），它转而学习当前活跃子任务的Q值。这缩短了价值预测范围，并使得使用时序差分（TD）目标进行有效学习成为可能。在训练过程中，离线机器人数据中存在的子任务级标注提供了分解，并使得能够从广泛且可能次优的机器人数据集中学习。为了在测试时消除对人类标注或模块化子任务预测系统的需求，我们的Q函数架构被训练为在估计其价值之前，自回归地以自然语言预测活跃子任务。我们使用基础视觉-语言骨干网络实例化SeeQ，在多样化的开源机器人操作数据上进行预训练，并在下游任务上微调。在两个双臂机器人平台上的四个真实世界操作任务中，SeeQ价值函数显著改善了最佳N策略引导。

papers.title: ForceTwin: Physics-informed Digital Twins for Robotic Manipulation from Instrumented Human Interaction
papers.title_zh: ForceTwin：基于仪器化人类交互的机器人操作物理信息数字孪生
papers.tldr_zh: ForceTwin通过人类交互力传感识别物理数字孪生，提升机器人操作成功率。
papers.cover_zh: 视觉一样的门，力气差很多？ForceTwin让机器人学会真实物理
papers.abstract_zh: 操作物体不仅需要理解其运动，还需要理解决定运动的物理属性。对于铰接物体，这些属性包括惯性、摩擦以及弹簧或闭门器等机构，其效果可能随配置和速度变化。这些属性无法从外观直接观察：视觉上相同的门可能需要截然不同的力来操作。现有的数字孪生流程主要恢复运动学或从视觉和语言先验分配静态物理参数，这可能导致物理上不合理的估计。因此，状态相关的机构动力学仍未被识别，也未在标准资产格式中表示。我们提出 ForceTwin，一个从仪器化人类交互中识别铰接物体物理信息数字孪生的系统。操作者使用手持力传感夹爪探测物体，提供同步的位姿和交互力，我们从中估计铰接、参数化动力学（包括惯性、库仑摩擦、粘性阻尼）以及捕获状态相关机构力的结构化神经残差。ForceTwin 将惯性参数误差比 VLM 先验几乎减半。作为 Spot 和 Franka FR3 上阻抗控制的前馈动力学模型，ForceTwin 在九个物体-具身对中实现了 87% 的目标完成率，而使用 VLM 先验和仅运动学孪生分别为 60% 和 57%，在具有强机构导致两个基线均停滞的物体上增益最大。我们进一步使用识别出的孪生训练全身开门策略并在真实世界中部署。项目页面：https://timengelbracht.github.io/forcetwin-website/

papers.title: Adaptive Rollout Truncation Based on Epistemic Uncertainty for Efficient Offline World Model Training
papers.title_zh: Adaptive Rollout Truncation Based on Epistemic Uncertainty for Efficient Offline World Model Training
papers.tldr_zh: Accurate neural world models are central to model-based robo
papers.cover_zh: Accurate neural world models are central to model-based robo
papers.abstract_zh: Accurate neural world models are central to model-based robotics, where they enable robots to predict future states from previously observed trajectories. Multi-step autoregressive training improves long-horizon prediction, but fixed rollout horizons also increase computational cost and can amplify early training errors when the model is still inaccurate. Existing training schemes typically use the same rollout length throughout optimization, independent of the model's current predictive reliability. We propose an epistemic uncertainty-driven adaptive rollout strategy for offline world model training following an auto-curriculum training scheme. Instead of always unrolling to a fixed horizon, the model terminates autoregressive rollouts once epistemic uncertainty exceeds a threshold calibrated from a warm-up phase. We study two uncertainty estimators: a five-head ensemble with a shared recurrent backbone and Monte Carlo Dropout. A two-stage warm-up procedure stabilizes uncertainty estimates before we enable adaptive truncation. Experiments on ANYmal-D and ANT show that ensemble-based adaptive truncation matches or improves the prediction accuracy of fixed-horizon training and the RWM-U baseline while requiring substantially fewer cumulative rollout steps. Training a world model on ANYmal-D following the presented approach reaches comparable final performance with the baselines with roughly 72% less rollout computation. These results indicate that epistemic uncertainty is useful not only for downstream policy regularization, but also for making world model training itself more compute-efficient.

papers.title: A Sim-to-Real Integration Pipeline for Training and Deployment of Chunk-Based VLA Manipulation Policies
papers.title_zh: 面向基于块VLA操作策略训练与部署的仿真到现实集成流水线
papers.tldr_zh: 开源仿真到现实协议，用仿真轨迹回放收集真实数据并评估VLA策略。
papers.cover_zh: 仿真数据直接训真机？这个开源协议让VLA落地不再烧钱
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型已成为将多模态输入（包括语义指令、场景视觉观测和本体感觉观测）映射到机器人动作的重要范式。大多数最先进的模型在末端执行器位姿空间中预测动作块序列。训练和评估这些模型需要大规模收集真实世界演示数据，将机器人动作与相应的视觉和本体感觉观测配对。在真实硬件上收集此类数据通常依赖人工遥操作，使得过程成本高昂、耗时且难以扩展。我们提出一个开源的仿真到现实实验协议来解决这一瓶颈：在仿真中生成的专家轨迹在真实的Franka FR3设置上开环回放，记录相应的真实视觉和本体感觉观测，并转换为与VLA训练兼容的格式。然后，相同的部署栈被复用，以闭环方式在该设置上评估训练好的策略，使得数据收集和评估共享相同的硬件配置。由于每个真实记录都与产生它的仿真轨迹配对，该协议还直接测量了仿真到现实的差距。我们在Hugging Face上发布了收集的数据集以及流水线源代码 https://gitlab.isir.upmc.fr/kappel/sim2real_public_chunk_control。

papers.title: Skel-WAM: A Hand-Skeleton-Conditioned World Action Model for Human-to-Robot Manipulation Transfer
papers.title_zh: Skel-WAM: A Hand-Skeleton-Conditioned World Action Model for Human-to-Robot Manipulation Transfer
papers.tldr_zh: Robot demonstrations are expensive to collect and often prov
papers.cover_zh: Robot demonstrations are expensive to collect and often prov
papers.abstract_zh: Robot demonstrations are expensive to collect and often provide limited distributional coverage of task variations. Human videos offer a low-cost source of complementary manipulation experience, but learning from them requires bridging embodiment gaps in visual appearance and action spaces. We introduce Skel-WAM, a world action model that bridges these differences through a unified hand-skeleton motion interface. The key insight is to align human and robot motion through a common hand topology, combining skeleton overlays that ground motion in the scene with structured 2.5-D keypoints that encode explicit hand kinematics. Video and Keypoint Experts jointly learn visual and skeletal dynamics through a Mixture-of-Transformers, while a separate robot-trained Action Expert maps these predictions to executable controls. This separation enables human and robot demonstrations to directly supervise shared dynamics without requiring robot action labels for human videos. Across four real-world bimanual tasks and seven simulated tasks, Skel-WAM achieves average success rates of 79.86% and 63.29%, surpassing the strongest baseline by 22.22 and 8.28 percentage points, respectively. Human-robot cotraining more than doubles real-world success on task variations absent from robot training data, from 38.89% to 86.11%. These results demonstrate that a shared skeletal interface enables joint learning across human and robot data and expands robot task coverage through complementary human demonstrations.

papers.title: FORTE: Task-Adaptive Force Capability Optimization for Mobile Manipulators
papers.title_zh: FORTE: Task-Adaptive Force Capability Optimization for Mobile Manipulators
papers.tldr_zh: Effective physical interaction control in robotic manipulati
papers.cover_zh: Effective physical interaction control in robotic manipulati
papers.abstract_zh: Effective physical interaction control in robotic manipulation requires not only kinematically feasible motion but also sufficient force-interaction capability. Existing redundancy resolution methods often ignore task-specific force demands or maximize the force capability indiscriminately, sacrificing dexterity when large force margins are unnecessary. We propose a task-oriented force capability optimization framework for redundant mobile manipulators. A Vision-Language Model (VLM) infers object physical properties from an RGB image and a task description, generating a desired task-force sequence that captures gravitational and inertial demands. We then define a task-oriented force capability metric as the signed distance between a task-force uncertainty ball and the dynamic residual force polytope (RFP), quantifying compatibility between task demands and the robot's remaining actuation capacity. This metric is incorporated, alongside manipulability, joint-limit avoidance, trajectory smoothness, and base-oscillation suppression, into a whole-body multi-objective trajectory-optimization problem. Experiments on a mobile manipulator performing lifting and single-point-holding tasks under varying payload conditions demonstrate that the proposed method provides sufficient force capability for heavy loads while preserving high manipulability for light loads. This yields a task-adaptive balance that fixed capability-maximizing baselines (RFP inscribed radius, RFP cone) and manipulability-only optimization fail to achieve. The core implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/yeying256/FORTE.

papers.title: Outcome-Conditioned End-Effector Geometry Across Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.title_zh: Outcome-Conditioned End-Effector Geometry Across Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies solve the same manipul
papers.cover_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies solve the same manipul
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies solve the same manipulation task through different action interfaces, but task success alone does not establish whether their physical executions agree. We study cross-policy end-effector geometry in 15,000 closed-loop LIBERO rollouts from four policies. The primary clean-condition analysis forms 3,600 configuration-matched, and therefore dependent, policy pairs. Both-success pairs have a median normalized dynamic time warping distance of 0.0120 m versus 0.0380 m when exactly one policy succeeds. This ordering holds in every task, every policy pair, and nine sampling and band-limited representations; however, the ratio varies severalfold across representations, so we report the direction rather than a fixed multiple. Both-failure pairs are more separated again but rest on thin, uneven support, so we report them as exploratory. Within successful executions, partner replacements separate more across tasks than across initial states. A matched baseline still reveals measurable, heterogeneous residual policy differences, so a low cross-policy distance does not imply interchangeability. Successful executions sit about as far from same-task demonstrations as those demonstrations sit from each other, compatible with task-associated geometry without separating training-data overlap from task constraints. A common 72-action window preserves the ordering but reduces its magnitude; endpoint and duration adjustment likewise leaves a positive mixed-outcome coefficient relative to both-success pairs, though its magnitude is specification-dependent. Under composite visual stress, policy rankings and pair composition change together.

papers.title: Towards Fine-Grained Object Manipulation: SAM3-Guided Visuomotor Policy with Persistent Memory Learning and Focused Visual Conditioning
papers.title_zh: Towards Fine-Grained Object Manipulation: SAM3-Guided Visuomotor Policy with Persistent Memory Learning and Focused Visual Conditioning
papers.tldr_zh: Fine-grained object (FO) manipulation requires robots to dis
papers.cover_zh: Fine-grained object (FO) manipulation requires robots to dis
papers.abstract_zh: Fine-grained object (FO) manipulation requires robots to distinguish a specified FO from visually similar objects and execute actions reliably despite scene distractors. However, scene-level visual conditioning lacks explicit object selection, while category-level guidance cannot reliably distinguish FOs within the same category. We present a SAM3-guided visuomotor framework that addresses these challenges through persistent object memory and focused visual conditioning. First, we introduce FO Memory-driven SAM3 (FOM-SAM3), which learns reusable FO memory tokens from limited multi-view registration images while keeping SAM3 fully frozen. Through one-vs-rest learning, these tokens encode persistent memories for localizing target FOs and rejecting similar alternatives, which can be stored in a memory bank. Second, we propose Focused Spatial-Appearance Encoding (FSAE), which combines in-FO local appearance features with explicit bounding-box coordinates to condition action policies including Diffusion Policy (DP) and Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT). The effectiveness of the proposed FOM-SAM3 was validated on the FO-30 dataset comprising 30 physical objects across four coarse categories. Across three real-robot FO manipulation tasks, our FOM-SAM3-guided policies demonstrated robustness against distractors, discrimination ability among similar FOs, and extendibility to new FOs.

papers.title: CommitFlow: Semantic Commitment Verification and Local Correction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation VLA Execution
papers.title_zh: CommitFlow：面向长时程机器人操作VLA执行的语义承诺验证与局部修正
papers.tldr_zh: CommitFlow通过语义承诺监控与局部修正，提升长时程机器人操作成功率。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人长时程任务总翻车？CommitFlow用语义承诺监控+局部修正，成功率直接起飞
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略已取得快速进展，长时程执行仍可能在所需物理效果建立之前就推进到下一任务阶段。我们将这种现象称为语义承诺（即一个阶段必须建立或维持的物理条件）与实际物理状态之间的不匹配。由于仅凭动作命令无法确认此类条件，局部偏差可能传播并导致任务失败。为解决该问题，我们提出CommitFlow，一种闭环执行框架，将承诺监控与局部修正相结合，同时保持基础策略冻结。CommitFlow集成了三个组件：语义承诺监控器（SCM）将阶段要求与当前状态证据进行比较，并在所需条件未满足或被违反时阻止依赖动作；BoundaryFlow随后基于当前状态和基础动作生成局部修正；关系与增益校准（RGC）选择满足相关约束的最小修正强度。在RoboTwin 2.0的十个常见基准任务上，CommitFlow平均成功率达到75.9%，相比基础策略pi0.5提升了22.7%。跨策略实验显示出一致增益，指向可靠的长时程机器人执行。

papers.title: Robotic Multiphase Interaction: Manipulating Coupled Liquid and Solid Dynamics with a World Model
papers.title_zh: Robotic Multiphase Interaction: Manipulating Coupled Liquid and Solid Dynamics with a World Model
papers.tldr_zh: This work presents textit{Robotic Multiphase Interaction (RM
papers.cover_zh: This work presents textit{Robotic Multiphase Interaction (RM
papers.abstract_zh: This work presents textit{Robotic Multiphase Interaction (RMI)}, a setting in which liquid enters a porous material and interacts mechanically with its deforming solid skeleton. Manipulation can therefore change pore volume, expel or redistribute retained liquid, and alter grasp stability at the same time. Spilled liquid can also create safety risks in domestic and manufacturing settings. This differs from most manipulation of solid objects and from tasks that involve both liquid and solid while keeping the phases spatially separate. We study a sponge filled with water as the first RMI example. We use implicit incompressible porous flow with smoothed particle hydrodynamics as the dynamics engine and enable robotic manipulation by adding Coulomb contact memory, hybrid velocity and force regulation, and a stability gate for lifting. The resulting environment connects robot commands to changes in the coupled liquid and solid state. A world model conditioned on actions predicts how this state evolves under candidate commands, while a temporal UNet generates actions using either Diffusion Policy or rectified flow matching. Our world model reduces retained water prediction error by more than $60\%$ compared with the baseline. The best action sequence selected by the world model from policy proposals further reduces the predicted terminal water error by about half. These improvements show that modelling the coupled liquid and solid state helps the robot predict how its actions affect both the porous object and the liquid held inside.

papers.title: Learning Distance-Conditioned Object Transport for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from a Single Motion Clip
papers.title_zh: Learning Distance-Conditioned Object Transport for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from a Single Motion Clip
papers.tldr_zh: Motion tracking can reproduce humanoid loco-manipulation fro
papers.cover_zh: Motion tracking can reproduce humanoid loco-manipulation fro
papers.abstract_zh: Motion tracking can reproduce humanoid loco-manipulation from a single retargeted motion clip, but a policy trained on a fixed reference primarily reproduces its demonstrated transport outcome. Although the source trajectory visits intermediate object displacements, transport termination is demonstrated only at its endpoint. We identify this mismatch as the termination-versus-passage gap: intermediate displacements are observed as passage states rather than termination-complete outcomes. We introduce Distance-Conditioned Reference Recomposition (DCRR), which relocates the demonstrated termination segment to intermediate transport states. A frozen tracking teacher replays the recomposed references under closed-loop dynamics, and the retained trajectories are relabeled by their achieved object placements and distilled into a reference-free policy. This procedure constructs distance-conditioned supervision from the interaction behavior encoded in the source motion. Across Carry, Kick-Push, Crouch-Push, and Drag, DCRR-BC produces command-dependent transport with an overall normalized distance mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.15, compared with 0.28 for source-only behavior cloning. RL fine-tuning further improves the command response and execution robustness in the training simulator and under sim-to-sim transfer. Finally, hardware experiments demonstrate transport-distance modulation across all four interaction modes.

papers.title: SABER: Learning Attention-based Semantic Affordance for Legged Locomotion
papers.title_zh: SABER: Learning Attention-based Semantic Affordance for Legged Locomotion
papers.tldr_zh: Perceptive legged locomotion has advanced rapidly by integra
papers.cover_zh: Perceptive legged locomotion has advanced rapidly by integra
papers.abstract_zh: Perceptive legged locomotion has advanced rapidly by integrating terrain geometry into learned policies, yet the integration of terrain meaning remains sparse: a pipe, a patch of grass, or a fragile box may be geometrically traversable while being inappropriate for contact. In industrial environments, where legged robots increasingly operate, a single misplaced step can damage fragile equipment, destabilize the robot, or endanger the site. To address this, we introduce SABER, a planner-free reinforcement-learning policy that jointly reasons about terrain geometry and semantic contact permission. The policy consumes a unified terrain-affordance map, where each cell encodes local 3D geometry and a semantic contact cost. We augment cross-attention with a learned, signed semantic bias: an additive term on the attention logits, gated by the contact cost, that reweights flagged cells by their distance from the nearest foot. A hazard therefore reshapes attention where it can still affect the next foothold, and its influence fades where it cannot. The resulting policy selects footholds on permitted support and keeps the leg clear of forbidden regions throughout the swing phase. We perform a systematic ablation that isolates the contribution of each architectural component; removing the semantic bias alone increases forbidden contacts by 55% while velocity tracking is unchanged. We validate the policy on a Unitree B2, demonstrating sim-to-real semantic contact selection across indoor and outdoor environments and four semantic obstacle classes.

papers.title: SynthDemo-RL: Breaking the Zero-Reward Barrier in VLA Adaptation with LLM-Guided Synthetic Demonstrations
papers.title_zh: SynthDemo-RL: Breaking the Zero-Reward Barrier in VLA Adaptation with LLM-Guided Synthetic Demonstrations
papers.tldr_zh: Fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models commonly rel
papers.cover_zh: Fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models commonly rel
papers.abstract_zh: Fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models commonly relies on human teleoperation demonstrations, while reinforcement learning (RL) with sparse binary rewards faces an exploration challenge when successful trajectories are rarely sampled. We propose SynthDemo-RL, a teacher-student framework in which an automated teacher converts simulator-privileged state into successful manipulation trajectories, a VLA student is distilled from them by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and PPO with binary task-success rewards refines the student. We study reward coverage, the fraction of tasks for which at least one success is observed under the fixed evaluation protocol, as a complement to the average success rate. On LIBERO-PRO, a public benchmark of perturbed LIBERO tasks for which no demonstrations exist, 27 of 57 scored tasks are at exactly 0% success for a pi_0.5 policy fine-tuned on the original LIBERO tasks. Direct PPO from this policy, under the same PPO recipe and the same RL compute as SynthDemo-RL's refinement stage, rescues 10 of these 27 tasks and leaves 17 at 0%. SynthDemo-RL, with 50 synthesized trajectories per task and no new human demonstrations, rescues all 27 and reaches average success rates of 97.8% and 97.1% on the Position and Task axes of LIBERO-PRO, respectively. On standard LIBERO, the same pipeline reaches 96.0% with no human demonstrations, within 1.7 points of pi_0.5 trained on 50 human demonstrations per task. We further validate the pipeline on RoboTwin 2.0 and verify that trajectories from a policy trained in a MuJoCo twin execute open-loop on a physical robot.

papers.title: Sandwich-Residuals: Parameter-Efficient Test-time Adaptation of World Models
papers.title_zh: Sandwich-Residuals：世界模型的参数高效测试时自适应
papers.tldr_zh: 冻结世界模型，仅学残差修正，实现高效测试时自适应。
papers.cover_zh: 冻结世界模型，只学小残差｜测试时自适应竟如此高效
papers.abstract_zh: 潜在世界模型通过在学到的表示空间中预测动作效果来实现规划，但当测试时条件与训练不同时，其预测可能变得不可靠。现有的测试时自适应方法通过更新预训练模型的部分参数来解决这一问题，通常需要修改数百万参数，并且需要选择适应哪些内部组件。我们提出 Sandwich-Residuals，一种轻量级替代方案，它保持预训练世界模型冻结，仅学习预测器周围的小型残差修正。这些残差利用模型的自监督预测误差在线优化，不需要奖励、标签或源域数据。在 AdaJEPA 基准的 21 种条件下，我们的方法达到了冻结模型成功率的 1.3 倍，同时保持了最强 AdaJEPA 变体 95% 的性能，并且自适应参数减少了 97-99%。在复合偏移下，这一优势增加到冻结模型成功率的 1.9 倍，同时与内部块自适应相当。我们进一步在用于 3-D 操作的 DINO-WM 模型上展示了相同的自适应原理。这些结果表明，世界模型的有效测试时自适应不一定需要修改其预训练的内部权重。

papers.title: From Pretraining to Proficiency: Real-World Subtask RL for Long-Horizon Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention
papers.title_zh: 从预训练到精通：面向长时程操作的现实世界子任务强化学习，极少人工干预
papers.tldr_zh: PARTS 框架通过子任务 RL 微调，以极少人工干预提升长时程操作成功率。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人总在关键步骤翻车？PARTS 让预训练策略直接精通
papers.abstract_zh: 预训练的机器人基础策略可能能执行长时程任务的大部分，但会在少数关键子任务上反复失败。收集额外的全任务演示进行监督微调（SFT）需要操作员重复策略已经表现良好的行为。强化学习（RL）微调提供了弥合这一差距的有前景的路径，但现有方法难以仅使用稀疏奖励解决长时程任务。我们提出了 PARTS（Policy Adaptation with RL on Targeted Subtasks），一个现实世界子任务 RL 框架，将练习集中在这些瓶颈上，同时允许训练 rollout 以极少人工干预进行。冻结的预训练策略在整个执行过程中提供标称动作，而智能体生成的选择器和成功验证器激活残差修正并提供局部结果奖励。这些奖励支持从成功子任务中学习，即使完整任务成功很少。训练结合在线 RL 与成功重加权再训练，每个再训练的残差策略被重新部署以收集进一步经验。人类在设置期间识别瓶颈并在需要时执行物理重置。在双臂 YAM 和单臂 Franka 任务上，PARTS 分别将完整任务成功率从 32% 提高到 61% 和从 50% 提高到 95%，平均每个任务使用数十分钟的现实世界 RL rollout。与现有的现实世界 RL 微调方法相比，PARTS 在相同的机器人 rollout 预算下将全任务成功率提高超过 25%，同时需要更少的人工参与。

papers.title: Contact-Rich Motion Planning via GPU-Parallel Mode Evaluation
papers.title_zh: 基于GPU并行模式评估的富接触运动规划
papers.tldr_zh: GPU并行评估接触模式，实现高效富接触运动规划。
papers.cover_zh: 终于不用绕开接触模式了｜GPU并行评估让规划又快又准
papers.abstract_zh: 富接触运动规划（CRMP）对机器人操作和运动至关重要，但由于组合接触决策而仍然计算困难。现有方法通常通过搜索启发式或优化重构来避免对接触模式序列的广泛评估。我们基于现代GPU硬件重新审视广泛评估，并引入接触模式扩展与并行轨迹优化（CoMET），它将GPU并行轨迹评估与贪心接触模式扩展相结合。在平面推动基准测试中，CoMET在解质量和规划时间上与基于优化、采样和树搜索的基线方法具有竞争力，在几乎所有实例上匹配全枚举参考，且评估次数更少、规划时间更短。消融实验表明，大部分性能提升来自高吞吐量轨迹评估器。在双臂非抓取操作中，随着模式空间增长，GPU友好的局部模式扩展比测试的自适应树搜索实现了更高的规划成功率。这些结果表明，广泛的显式模式评估为CRMP提供了一种简单而有效的替代方案。

papers.title: Duty Factor Predicts Robust Constrained Quadrupedal Locomotion Across Gait Types
papers.title_zh: 占空比预测跨步态类型的鲁棒约束四足运动
papers.tldr_zh: 占空比比步态类型更能预测四足运动的鲁棒性。
papers.cover_zh: 步态类型不重要？占空比才是四足机器人鲁棒运动的关键！
papers.abstract_zh: 四足机器人越来越多地部署在需要运动对干扰和受限地形保持鲁棒的环境中。步态类型（如行走或小跑）通常用于表征四足运动。然而，步态类型并不能唯一地定义运动，因为占空比、速度和站立宽度等参数可以在单一歩态类型内变化。在这项工作中，我们使用三种不同的四足运动控制方法研究了这些步态参数之间的关系。首先，使用带有LQR反馈的全身轨迹优化，我们表明占空比比标称步态类型更能预测局部误差收敛。其次，我们通过学习的运动控制器研究占空比选择，表明占空比如何作为一种低维参数来适应狭窄地形环境中的运动鲁棒性。最后，我们表明这些趋势在质心模型预测控制框架下持续存在，并通过在物理四足上的狭窄地形实验验证了它们。这些结果表明，占空比为理解和选择跨步态类型和控制架构的鲁棒四足运动提供了一个简单而有效的基础。

papers.title: CRISP: Contact-Rich Robotic Simulation Platform with Extensive Geometries and Contact Solvers
papers.title_zh: CRISP：面向复杂接触的机器人仿真平台，支持丰富几何表示与接触求解器
papers.tldr_zh: 提出高保真机器人仿真平台CRISP，支持丰富几何与鲁棒接触求解。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人仿真总穿模？这个新平台专治复杂接触
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出了 CRISP（Contact-RIch Simulation Platform），一个面向复杂多接触仿真（如紧公差机器人操作）的高保真物理引擎。在机器人仿真中实现高物理保真度，既需要对几何和接触交互进行富有表现力的建模，也需要通过鲁棒的碰撞检测和接触求解器进行精确的数值求解。然而，现有仿真器通常要么对几何表示的支持有限且接触交互建模简化，要么采用的数值求解方法在精度或鲁棒性上存在固有局限。为此，我们开发了一个新的仿真器，它支持多种几何表示并具备基于优化的精确碰撞检测，同时将接触建模与鲁棒的增广拉格朗日接触求解器相结合。这种集成能够在复杂几何体之间高效且一致地检测接触信息，同时精确求解多接触约束而无需引入有问题的松弛，这对于仿真接触密集和尖锐交互至关重要。我们通过与最先进平台对比验证了仿真器的物理保真度，并通过复杂机器人操作场景进一步展示了其能力。CRISP 已在 https://github.com/INRoL/crisp 公开可用。

papers.title: Benchmarking World Models for Continual Learning on Compositional Tasks
papers.title_zh: 面向组合任务持续学习的世界模型基准测试
papers.tldr_zh: 提出组合持续学习基准，评估世界模型在机器人操作中的知识重用与遗忘。
papers.cover_zh: 模块化世界模型竟能平衡重用与遗忘？但问题还没完全解决！
papers.abstract_zh: 世界模型的一个理想特性是能够跨任务持续学习，适应新环境而不遗忘智能体已学到的知识。特别是，保留和重用从先前经验中获得的知识的能力，支撑了智能体高效适应新环境的能力，因为物理世界的动态通常可以用重复出现的机制来描述。然而，世界模型的适应度量纠缠了两种能力：学习未见任务的速度和容量，以及重用已获得的知识，因为新任务在带来新内容的同时也包含重复出现的部分。为了将知识重用从先前经验中分离出来，我们提出了一个用于机器人操作中世界模型的组合持续学习基准。具体来说，我们为每个任务课程设计组合任务，这些任务结合了序列中已见任务的各个方面。我们进一步沿动作和感知轴对这种组合进行分解，以更好地理解不同输入模态如何瓶颈知识重用。我们在典型的持续学习方法下评估了最先进的世界模型，以及一个模块化世界模型，其动态主干包含显式可重用的组件。结果表明，模块化在重用与遗忘之间比传统方法平衡得更好，但都没有完全解决问题，为构建能够重用而不遗忘的持续世界模型留下了明确的空间。更多细节请访问我们的项目网站：https://object814.github.io/Compositional-Continual-Learning/。

papers.title: Visual Proactivity: Enhancing Human-Robot Collaboration Through Intent Communication
papers.title_zh: Visual Proactivity: Enhancing Human-Robot Collaboration Through Intent Communication
papers.tldr_zh: As robots transition from performing repetitive tasks to col
papers.cover_zh: As robots transition from performing repetitive tasks to col
papers.abstract_zh: As robots transition from performing repetitive tasks to collaborating with humans, understanding human intent becomes crucial to effective interaction. Anticipation enables robots to predict human actions, while proactivity allows them to take initiative and guide human behavior toward optimal outcomes. Although research has largely focused on how robots infer and respond to human intentions, less attention has been paid to how robots communicate their own intent. This paper introduces visual proactivity, a novel, simple yet effective approach that enables robots to communicate their intentions through visual feedback, influencing human behavior and enhancing transparency and fluency. We develop and evaluate proactive robotic behaviors in a human-to-robot handover scenario, where a user study validates human perception of reactive, anticipatory, and proactive behaviors. The results demonstrate that effective visual proactivity fosters better alignment and coordination, paving the way for more intuitive human-robot collaboration.

papers.title: Beyond Kinematics: Benchmarking Simulation Fidelity for Muscle-Driven Imitation Learning
papers.title_zh: 超越运动学：面向肌肉驱动模仿学习的仿真保真度基准测试
papers.tldr_zh: 比较两种运动模仿强化学习流程，HyFyDy 的肌肉激活更接近实验 EMG。
papers.cover_zh: 运动学准就够了吗？肌肉激活才是关键｜仿真保真度大比拼
papers.abstract_zh: 在本工作中，我们对两种最先进的运动模仿强化学习（MIRL）流程进行了系统性比较，一种基于 SCONE/HyFyDy，另一种基于 MuJoCo/MyoSim。HyFyDy 通过详细的肌肉肌腱建模强调生理真实性，而 MuJoCo 优先考虑计算效率和可扩展的策略学习。尽管近期工作表明这两种流程都能高保真地复现人体运动学，但它们是否能准确捕捉产生运动的潜在神经肌肉行为仍不清楚。这一局限性对于机器人辅助设备的设计和控制尤为重要，因为肌肉激活模式和代谢成本等结果指标常被用作优化目标。为了进行系统性比较，我们的工作使用一组共同的人体运动捕捉和肌电图（EMG）测量数据来比较这两种流程。结果发现，虽然两种流程都能以相对精度产生相似的运动学，但 HyFyDy 的肌肉激活与实验 EMG 更为一致，这由 HyFyDy 和 MuJoCo 肌肉激活的平均池化（RMSE, r）值支持：分别为 (0.164, 0.4) 和 (0.344, 0.11)。我们得出结论，HyFyDy 更先进的生理真实性目前使其更适合肌肉骨骼建模，但两者都需要进一步发展，以将生理真实性带入 GPU 可并行化的仿真环境，并推动机器人辅助设备设计。

papers.title: ME-Dex 1.0: Bringing Heterogeneous Tactile Sensing into World Action Modeling
papers.title_zh: ME-Dex 1.0: Bringing Heterogeneous Tactile Sensing into World Action Modeling
papers.tldr_zh: World Action Models bring the predictive capabilities of vid
papers.cover_zh: World Action Models bring the predictive capabilities of vid
papers.abstract_zh: World Action Models bring the predictive capabilities of video models into robot action generation, providing a rich foundation for modeling future visual states. Tactile sensing complements this foundation with direct measurements of physical interaction. Some existing methods use tactile features as conditioning inputs without jointly predicting future tactile states, visual observations, and actions. Our key insight is that tactile signals, like video, provide observations of the evolving world state and should be modeled as future observations alongside video. We present ME-Dex-1.0 (MachEmbodied-Dex-1.0), a unified World Action Tactile Model for joint visual, tactile, and action learning. ME-Dex-1.0 adopts a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture comprising a Video Expert, a Tactile Expert, and an Action Expert, all trained with flow matching. We use shared attention connects the experts in intermediate layers, allowing action generation to draw on learned representations of visual and tactile dynamics during joint denoising. To support multi-source heterogeneous tactile inputs, a Canonical Hand Model and a Unified Tactile Autoencoder map tactile observations from different embodiments and sensing layouts into shared spatial and latent spaces. To address the limited availability of paired visual, tactile, and action data, we develop the Agentic Tactile Data Engine, an agent-based data production platform. It supplements RoboTwin and DexJoCo with tactile data recorded directly from force sensors during trajectory replay in simulation. Experiments on the RoboTwin, DexJoCo, and ManiFeel simulation platforms, together with real robot evaluations, demonstrate improved manipulation performance using both grippers and dexterous hands equipped with tactile sensing.

papers.title: ZeroTouch: Tactile-Supervised Visual Contact Estimation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.title_zh: ZeroTouch: Tactile-Supervised Visual Contact Estimation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.tldr_zh: Reliable robotic grasping benefits from estimating the evolv
papers.cover_zh: Reliable robotic grasping benefits from estimating the evolv
papers.abstract_zh: Reliable robotic grasping benefits from estimating the evolving physical interaction and selecting a grasp-dependent compression target. Tactile sensors provide direct interaction measurements but require dedicated hardware at deployment. We introduce ZeroTouch, a tactile-supervised framework that predicts dense contact deformation, the instantaneous six-axis wrench, and a grasp-dependent desired compression target from wrist RGB observations, gripper state, and local gravity direction. Tactile measurements are used only as privileged supervision during training and are not required at deployment. On the full validation set, the complete architecture reduces normal-force MAE from 2.017 N for a state-only baseline to 0.531 N. In physical evaluation with 20 trials per condition, ZeroTouch achieves 95% success on an unseen object, 80% in a seen-object/unseen-grasp condition, and 90% under a content/load shift. Under the same evaluation protocol, OpenVLA achieves 25%, 40%, and 55%, while SmolVLA achieves 10%, 25%, and 35%, respectively.

papers.title: Intervention Granularity Matters: Coherent Treatment Bundles in Counterfactual Simulation with Clinical World Models
papers.title_zh: 干预粒度很重要：临床世界模型反事实模拟中的连贯治疗组合
papers.tldr_zh: 临床世界模型中，干预粒度影响反事实模拟，完整治疗组合比单一设置更能改变预测。
papers.cover_zh: 干预粒度决定模拟成败？完整治疗组合让预测大不同
papers.abstract_zh: 基于临床世界模型的反事实模拟意味着固定患者病史、改变治疗并读取预测响应。这样做需要确定什么算作一次干预。在临床环境中，干预被记录为组合：对来自MIMIC-IV的945,707患者小时进行共现审计显示，某些组件组（如透析回路的每个参数）从未单独出现，因此单独改变一个组件的编辑描述了一个在数据中从未出现过的小时。我们假设编辑干预的粒度会改变世界模型的响应方式，并用Clin-JEPA（一种以每小时治疗文本为条件的患者轨迹潜在世界模型）进行测试。在1,019次有记录的侵入性通气开始时，我们保持患者病史和其他治疗不变，比较编辑一个呼吸机设置与编辑为最近轨迹最相似的真实患者记录的完整配置。完整组合比任何单一设置更能推动预测的下一状态，在所有五个设置上一致，并且在考虑每次编辑改变模型输入的程度后差异仍然存在。因此，干预粒度实质性地影响临床世界模型的响应：单组件编辑可能低估治疗敏感性，而组合感知编辑可能为反事实治疗模拟提供更有支持的基础。

papers.title: GALA: Geometry-Aware Latent Action Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Model Pretraining across Embodiments
papers.title_zh: GALA：面向跨具身视觉-语言-动作模型预训练的几何感知潜在动作建模
papers.tldr_zh: GALA用几何感知潜在动作提升跨具身VLA预训练。
papers.cover_zh: 手指级动作也能建模？GALA让跨具身预训练不再难
papers.abstract_zh: 从多具身数据集中学习大规模视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型仍然具有挑战性，因为不同末端执行器的动作空间存在异构性。尽管潜在动作模型（LAM）能够从多样化的视频数据中学习具身无关的动作表示，但现有的基于图像的LAM往往无法捕捉细粒度的末端执行器关节运动，尤其是人类和灵巧机器人手部的指级几何变化。为了解决这一局限，我们提出了GALA，一个几何感知的潜在动作建模框架，它通过3D末端执行器几何运动来增强基于图像的潜在动作。然而，简单地引入点云会产生细粒度动作表示，其共享语义有限，阻碍了跨具身预训练。为了解决这个问题，我们引入了统一末端执行器运动表示（UEMR），它在保留细粒度运动信息的同时提高了潜在动作的跨具身泛化能力。基于UEMR，GALA结合了捕捉场景级动态的视觉潜在动作和捕捉共享细粒度末端执行器关节运动的几何潜在动作，为从多具身数据（包括无动作的自我中心人类视频）中进行VLA预训练提供了有效的监督。在细粒度运动探测、跨具身检索和下游VLA评估上的实验表明，GALA在跨具身建模可泛化细粒度运动方面是有效的，达到了68.3%的RoboCasa-GR1成功率和75.5%的真实世界成功率。代码、附录和演示可在https://puzhenyuan.github.io/GALA-website/获取。

papers.title_zh: 面向并行仿真中机器人操作的视觉语言奖励学习扩展
papers.tldr_zh: RAPID系统通过并行仿真和单请求标注，大幅加速VLM奖励学习。
papers.cover_zh: 训练时间从9小时降到1小时？这个系统让机器人奖励学习直接起飞
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）可以替代人类标注者进行基于偏好的奖励学习，但顺序 API 请求和单环境数据收集使得训练缓慢且昂贵。我们提出 RAPID（基于自适应并行图像多样性的奖励学习），一个将 GPU 并行 rollout 与数据感知策略更新、单请求偏好标注、自动奖励稳定化和代表性图像采样相结合的系统。我们在 IsaacLab 中的五个 Franka Panda 操作任务上评估了这些组件。并行 rollout 和自适应更新首次实现了训练时间的显著减少：在匹配的两阶段提示下，平均运行时间从 9.18 小时降至 3.13 小时。启用所有 RAPID 组件后，训练在 1.15 小时内完成，每次运行使用 896 次而非 19,840 次 API 调用，总体最终成功率从 86.3% 提升至 98.7%。这代表了 8.0 倍的端到端加速和 95.5% 的 API 使用减少。使用 Gemma 3 12B 和 GPT-4.1 mini 的离线评估表明，单请求提示降低了两种模型的标注延迟和成本。代码见：https://github.com/rapid-vlm/rapid-vlm-rl。

papers.title: AcousticDiffusion: Semantically Conditioned Audio-Guided Diffusion Policy for Search-and-Rescue Assistance
papers.title_zh: AcousticDiffusion：面向搜救辅助的语义条件音频引导扩散策略
papers.tldr_zh: 音频引导扩散策略让搜救机器人更接近呼救者。
papers.cover_zh: 听声辨位新突破｜扩散策略让机器人精准找到呼救者
papers.abstract_zh: 在视觉接触退化或被遮挡的环境中，向人类呼救者导航是救援机器人的一项重要能力。我们提出 AcousticDiffusion，一种语义条件、音频引导的扩散策略，用于面向人类的导航。一个冻结的预训练音频识别器处理 10.24 秒的窗口，通过语音门控和遇险感知优先级将识别输出转换为源级导航角色。麦克风阵列的到达方向测量被递归地集成到以机器人为中心的贝叶斯鸟瞰图信念场中。自运动补偿对齐连续观测，在保持由方位引起的距离不确定性的同时逐步约束源位置。语义信念、近期声学观测、音频特征和机器人状态共同条件化一个扩散模型，该模型生成航点轨迹。在使用录制音频的合成导航验证集上，AcousticDiffusion 实现了 11.20 度的平均终点方位误差，91.78% 的轨迹与呼救者方向对齐在 30 度以内。干扰源拒绝率在 89.20% 到 98.99% 之间，策略在 91.07% 的窗口中优先选择标记为 HELP 的呼救者而非竞争说话者。在 ZSL-1 四足机器人上在线部署且无需额外重新训练，其平均方位误差为 64.9 度，而 A* 为 98.2 度，RRT 为 90.4 度，平均规划器计算时间为 6.07 毫秒。尽管声学定位不完美，报告的平均最终源距离从使用 ODAS（Open embedded Audition System）引导的经典规划器的 3.96 米减少到 2.48 米，提升了 37.4%。这些结果证明了该框架将不确定的声学观测转化为更接近人类呼救者的能力。

papers.title: MicroHookACT: Monocular Microscopic Vision Guided Visuomotor Policy for Flexible Microelectrode Hooking
papers.title_zh: MicroHookACT: Monocular Microscopic Vision Guided Visuomotor Policy for Flexible Microelectrode Hooking
papers.tldr_zh: Automated needle-loop hooking is a critical step in flexible
papers.cover_zh: Automated needle-loop hooking is a critical step in flexible
papers.abstract_zh: Automated needle-loop hooking is a critical step in flexible microelectrode (FME) implantation. This paper presents MicroHookACT, an imitation learning-based visuomotor policy for automated 3D hooking under monocular microscopic vision. First, a unidirectional hooking strategy exploits defocus cues and optical-axis guidance to enable palpation-free precise alignment and contact-rich threading. Second, an action-supervised object attention module built on a frozen ViT backbone learns to focus on the micro-needle tip and micro-loop directly from human demonstrations, without requiring manual visual annotations for training. Third, attention-centered global coarse and local fine features are dynamically weighted according to predicted action progress, enabling a single ACT policy to adapt to changing defocus blur and visual requirements throughout the operation. In the experiments, visuomotor policies were trained on 60 human demonstrations and evaluated under five setups with varying difficulties. Our MicroHookACT framework achieved the highest overall success rate of 96.7\% with an average execution time of 11.5 s. These results demonstrate the potential of visuomotor policy learning for micron-level control under varying operating conditions.

papers.title: MT-WAM: Reorienting the One-Pass Predictive Representation Toward Action Generation
papers.title_zh: MT-WAM: Reorienting the One-Pass Predictive Representation Toward Action Generation
papers.tldr_zh: Fast-WAM shows that video-action co-training improves contro
papers.cover_zh: Fast-WAM shows that video-action co-training improves contro
papers.abstract_zh: Fast-WAM shows that video-action co-training improves control without generating future video at inference, making the representation from a single video diffusion Transformer forward central to action generation. However, future-observation prediction does not explicitly prioritize the future dynamics and visual structure needed for control. We present MT-WAM, which retains the original training objectives and adds complementary supervision for future two-dimensional point trajectories and visual features. A lightweight dual-stream branch copied from the video backbone's final blocks provides target-specific processing, while a structured attention mask prevents cross-stream attention. Motion-stream tokens supply additional dynamics conditions to the action expert. Future visual-feature prediction provides supervision in a feature space that captures object and spatial structure. This supervision trains the video backbone to provide more informative visual context for action generation under changing visual conditions, without adding visual-feature-stream tokens to action conditioning. At inference, MT-WAM uses video and motion caches computed once per replan and skips future-video prediction. Without additional embodied policy pretraining, MT-WAM achieves 98.2% success on LIBERO and 73.7% on LIBERO-Plus, exceeding Fast-WAM by 23.8 percentage points on the latter. On RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Rand, Random success increases from 6.30% to 19.40%; across four real-world tasks, average success increases from 67.0% to 77.8%.

papers.title: Potential-Field Action Representation for Reinforcement Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.title_zh: Potential-Field Action Representation for Reinforcement Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.tldr_zh: Model-free reinforcement learning can acquire contact-rich r
papers.cover_zh: Model-free reinforcement learning can acquire contact-rich r
papers.abstract_zh: Model-free reinforcement learning can acquire contact-rich robotic manipulation skills through trial-and-error interaction, but it often requires the policy to learn both task strategy and low-level motion generation. In this setting, the action representation is critical because it determines how policy outputs are converted into robot motion, shaping both exploration and physical execution. Direct Cartesian command interfaces require the policy to generate motion at every decision step, coupling task-level adaptation with continuous low-level control and increasing the learning burden. We propose PA-RL, a reinforcement-learning framework that uses artificial potential fields as the action representation. Instead of commanding motion directly, the policy adapts the parameters of an energy-like potential field, which generates a state-dependent guidance direction executed through a Cartesian impedance controller. We evaluate PA-RL on peg-in-hole insertion, a representative contact-rich task with nonlinear dynamics and discontinuous contact transitions. In simulation, PA-RL is compared with Cartesian velocity, Cartesian pose, and variable-impedance action spaces using the same RL algorithm. PA-RL is the only method to reach a 100% evaluation success rate within the allotted training time, while the best baseline reaches 92.6%. It also reduces joint-torque variation by 55.4% and Cartesian acceleration variation by 70.8% relative to the best baseline, without explicit motion-quality penalties in the reward. The simulation-trained policy further completes 9/9 real-robot insertions without fine-tuning, demonstrating the deployment feasibility of the learned potential-field interface.

papers.title: PSR: Predictive Sensorimotor Representation Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.title_zh: PSR：面向富接触操作的预测性感觉运动表征学习
papers.tldr_zh: PSR 学习预测性感觉运动表征，提升富接触操作成功率。
papers.cover_zh: 主动预测接触力｜这个新框架让机器人操作精度飙升
papers.abstract_zh: 富接触操作要求策略在视觉观察之外，对接触力、机器人构型和交互历史进行推理，从而生成精确动作。现有方法被动地以力反馈为条件，而非主动预测未来的接触动力学，限制了其生成高精度动作的能力。为解决这一问题，我们提出了预测性感觉运动表征（PSR）学习，这是一个从多模态感觉运动信号中学习层次化预测表征，并将其集成到视觉运动策略动作流中的框架。具体而言，在预训练阶段，训练一个多模态 Transformer 通过联合预测未来交互动力学来学习层次化预测表征。学习到的层次结构随后增强动作流，使所得策略能够在多个深度上利用接触相关线索。我们进一步在视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型中实例化 PSR，得到 PSR-VLA，并在六个真实世界富接触操作任务上对其进行评估。实验结果表明，PSR-VLA 取得了 91.7% 的总体成功率，分别比 $π_{0.5}$、ForceVLA-$π_{0.5}$ 和 ForceVLA2-$π_{0.5}$ 高出 30.0、22.5 和 19.2 个百分点。这些结果证明了所提出的 PSR 在力感知、富接触操作中的有效性。任务视频和稳定性测试可在 https://psr-vla.pages.dev/ 获取。

papers.title: MAAP: Multi-Agent Active Perception for Collaborative Manipulation
papers.title_zh: MAAP：面向协作操作的多智能体主动感知
papers.tldr_zh: MAAP让每条机械臂在操作时兼作移动视角，结合角色感知模仿学习提升协作成功率。
papers.cover_zh: 机械臂边干活边当摄像头？协作操作竟成主动感知新范式
papers.abstract_zh: 多智能体操作天然产生多个任务驱动的视角：每条机械臂都携带腕部相机，并在执行动作的同时在场景中移动。然而这些观测通常未被充分利用，操作中的主动感知仍常被视为需要专门的感知智能体。我们提出MAAP（多智能体主动感知），其中每条机械臂都是双用途的：它执行操作动作，同时通过其携带的腕部相机，作为团队的移动视角。我们将其与RAIL（角色感知模仿学习）配对，后者预测每条机械臂当前的角色及其动作块，并以此作为动作生成的条件，在一个网络中表示角色相关的动作。在四个模拟任务中，拓宽感知机制将平均成功率从固定相机的56.5%提升至一个主动腕部视角的62.5%和全部主动视角的70.0%，而MAAP+RAIL达到79.2%。RAIL的额外增益集中在三臂微波炉任务上，在相同的多腕部输入下，成功率从47%升至82%。在双臂平台上，MAAP+RAIL在20次放置试验中成功14次，而固定视角ACT为0次。因此，协作操作本身可以作为一种主动感知机制。

papers.title: DPed-VLN: A Benchmark for Socially Compliant Vision-and-Language Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments
papers.title_zh: DPed-VLN: A Benchmark for Socially Compliant Vision-and-Language Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) has advanced rapidly in
papers.cover_zh: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) has advanced rapidly in
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) has advanced rapidly in static indoor environments, but robots operating in human-populated spaces must ground language while responding to moving pedestrians and social-safety constraints. We present DPed-VLN, a Habitat 3.0 benchmark for dynamic-pedestrian VLN that couples 33,093 navigation episodes with paired global and prior-augmented instructions, ORCA-controlled humanoid pedestrians, socially constrained expert paths, and metrics that jointly assess navigation efficiency and social safety. DPed-VLN separates ordinary goal-oriented route guidance from prior-augmented instructions that expose dynamic-pedestrian cues for controlled analysis. To instantiate the benchmark, we introduce DPet (Dynamic Pedestrian-aware Network), a pedestrian-aware policy network trained with reinforcement learning and imitation learning. We further adapt representative state-of-the-art VLM-based navigation models, including NaVILA and StreamVLN, to DPed-VLN through LoRA fine-tuning. Experiments show that LoRA adaptation improves zero-shot VLM baselines in several success and safety metrics, especially reducing StreamVLN's collision rate. Among the evaluated methods, DPet-RL achieves the highest SR, SPL, and STL.

papers.title: 2nd Place Solution to the HANDS 2026 Workshop Challenge-Dexterous Grasp Motion Track: Single-Shot Trajectory Warping for Grasp Motion Generation
papers.title_zh: 2nd Place Solution to the HANDS 2026 Workshop Challenge-Dexterous Grasp Motion Track: Single-Shot Trajectory Warping for Grasp Motion Generation
papers.tldr_zh: This report describes our 2nd place solution to the HANDS 20
papers.cover_zh: This report describes our 2nd place solution to the HANDS 20
papers.abstract_zh: This report describes our 2nd place solution to the HANDS 2026 workshop challenge (Dexterous Grasp Motion track) in conjunction with ECCV 2026. In this challenge, we address grasp motion generation for the 12-DoF LinkerHand O6, aiming to produce physically plausible reach-and-lift trajectories for unseen objects from randomized initial hand poses in simulation. This task is particularly challenging because each grasp requires a per-step policy to make approximately $70$ twelve-dimensional decisions, with errors accumulating over time, while test objects and physical dynamics may differ from those encountered during training. To address these challenges, we propose editing a single successful GraspM3 demonstration instead of generating the motion step by step: a policy observes the object once and outputs a 12-D warp of the demonstration, which is then replayed open-loop. Moreover, we train the warp policy with one-step PPO over all $4{,}824$ training objects in parallel. As a result, our method achieved success rates of $94.61\%$ on the easy track, the highest of all submissions, and $57.18\%$ on the hard track of the private test set.

papers.title: NeuRIO: A Streaming Neural Estimator for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Multi-Robot Relative Inertial Odometry
papers.title_zh: NeuRIO: A Streaming Neural Estimator for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Multi-Robot Relative Inertial Odometry
papers.tldr_zh: We present NeuRIO, a streaming neural estimator for anchor-f
papers.cover_zh: We present NeuRIO, a streaming neural estimator for anchor-f
papers.abstract_zh: We present NeuRIO, a streaming neural estimator for anchor-free 6-DoF relative inertial odometry using only identified inter-robot bearings, ranges, and IMU measurements. NeuRIO canonicalizes measurements into gravity-aligned coordinates, represents robots as nodes and mutual observations as factors, and uses attention for spatial reasoning and GRUs for temporal modeling. As a graph network, NeuRIO applies shared node-wise and factor-wise operators throughout the network, enabling it to handle different team sizes and time-varying observation graphs. NeuRIO is trained on a simulator that couples various motion patterns, device-level sensor characteristics, and diverse, realistic modeled, and temporally persistent sensor corruptions. In this way, NeuRIO achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. Across $24$ real-world sequences, NeuRIO achieves $14.1\,mathrm{cm}$ position RMSE and $3.9^circ$ rotation RMSE. More importantly, NeuRIO demonstrates strong computational scalability, maintaining an update cost below $20\,mathrm{ms}$ with up to $400$ robots in simulation, while optimization-based methods exceed $20\,mathrm{ms}$ at only $24$ robots. Moreover, even trained on limited team sizes, NeuRIO transfers directly to unseen larger teams without architectural or parameter changes.

papers.title: World Modeling in Transformers
papers.title_zh: Transformer 中的世界建模
papers.tldr_zh: Transformer 能学世界模型，失败源于特征干扰而非缺乏表征。
papers.cover_zh: Transformer 真的没有世界模型？机制分析揭开真相
papers.abstract_zh: 行为上的失败可能让一个 transformer 看起来缺乏世界模型，即使它已经学到了对其环境的忠实表征。我们在 TaxiGPT 中证明了这一点，这是一个在曼哈顿随机游走上训练的 transformer，其失败曾被解读为其内部地图不连贯的证据。通过机制分析和因果干预，我们表明该模型表征了交叉路口和街道，追踪其位置，并使用目标指南针进行导航。我们将其失败追溯到叠加的交叉路口特征之间的干扰，这种干扰破坏了内部地图中的定位。可供性打包（affordance packing）将具有相同合法移动的交叉路口的表征分组，有助于限制这些错误的后果。最后，我们提出了机制性指标，并用它们来比较模型，并表明世界建模能力在训练的不同阶段出现。我们的发现促使我们从一个模型是否有世界模型的问题，转向对其世界建模的机制性研究：即它通过哪些相互作用的能力来表征其环境，并利用这些表征来指导行为。

papers.title: Compact but Moving: Intervention-Relevant Geometry in Recurrent World Models
papers.title_zh: 紧凑但移动：循环世界模型中的干预相关几何
papers.tldr_zh: 循环世界模型中紧凑干预结构以移动局部几何形式持续存在。
papers.cover_zh: 高维循环状态里，紧凑干预竟会移动？新研究揭示反直觉几何
papers.abstract_zh: 学习到的世界模型即使循环状态是高维的，也可能具有紧凑的干预，但这样的校正进入模型后会发生什么尚不清楚。我们在一个受控的循环世界模型中研究这个问题，先前的工作为一次性反事实速度干预确定了一个检查点特定的秩-4接口。在自主展开过程中，校正迅速离开这个固定的入口子空间。然而，通过事实循环雅可比链传输入口方向得到的低秩图像继续捕获了大部分非线性校正。使用切线预测校正的重启保留了大量的反事实未来函数。这种传输/函数模式在独立训练的结构化GRU模型和参数匹配的LSTM中重复出现，后者用特权紧凑校正初始化。我们进一步刻画了全循环载体上的有限时域未来响应算子。修补将其主要的未来敏感方向转向匹配的本地反事实组织，并且局部算子准确地对修补和本地反事实基点上注册方向面板上的有限扰动效应进行排序。一个单独的全幅度测定发现了大量事实端点切线残差，并支持三个检查点中两个的响应重构。总之，这些结果表明，紧凑的干预结构可以作为嵌入高维循环动力学中的移动的、状态依赖的局部几何而持续存在，而不意味着一个固定的或动态封闭的低维状态。

papers.title: PRIME: Perception Feedback with Situational Memory Embeddings in VLA Models
papers.title_zh: PRIME: 在VLA模型中融入情境记忆嵌入的感知反馈
papers.tldr_zh: PRIME通过情境记忆反馈提升VLA感知，在Bench2Drive上取得最高驾驶得分。
papers.cover_zh: 感知不再盲目！PRIME让VLA模型用记忆反馈精准看路
papers.abstract_zh: 当前的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在自动驾驶中主要通过感知-推理-规划层次的前馈推理运行。尽管现代架构在感知模块内保持时间递归，但早期感知对下游推理和导航目标仍然盲目，处理视觉输入时无差别对待，没有根据先前决策提供的线索进行优先处理。为了弥合这一差距，本文提出了PRIME，一种学习到的反馈机制，通过新颖的情境记忆来调节VLA感知查询。通过交叉注意力聚合过去感知、推理、导航目标和预测行为的潜在表示，跨越L步窗口，PRIME以最小的计算成本实现了意图驱动的感知注意力，最多仅增加29.7M参数（占7.3B参数基础模型的0.41%）。在Bench2Drive闭环基准上评估，PRIME达到了最先进的驾驶得分82.47（比ORION高4.73）和成功率60.00%（提高5.38个百分点），这是在Think2Drive演示上训练的已发表VLA中报告的最高驾驶得分。

papers.title: ProTracer: Proprioception-Guided Failure Diagnosis in Robot Manipulation
papers.title_zh: ProTracer: Proprioception-Guided Failure Diagnosis in Robot Manipulation
papers.tldr_zh: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for robot mani
papers.cover_zh: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for robot mani
papers.abstract_zh: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for robot manipulation failure analysis that includes binary failure detection, failure categorization, explanation generation, and the additional capability of failure onset localization, which aims to identify the earliest moment at which a robot execution deviates from a valid task-completion trajectory and is ultimately followed by task failure. To address these tasks, we propose ProTracer, a training-free framework that leverages existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) together with proprioceptive signals for failure analysis. Our method uses proprioceptive dynamics to identify temporally informative action boundaries and converts richer robot-state signals into structured natural-language descriptions that can be jointly analyzed together with visual observations by the VLM. This design combines the temporal precision of proprioceptive signals with the multimodal reasoning capabilities of modern VLMs without requiring additional model training. We further introduce FailTime, a benchmark with synchronized visual and proprioceptive observations for evaluating conventional failure diagnosis tasks as well as failure onset localization. Experiments demonstrate that ProTracer achieves strong performance across both conventional failure diagnosis tasks and the newly introduced failure onset localization task, highlighting the importance of proprioceptive reasoning for fine-grained temporal failure analysis.

papers.title: Stabilizing Trajectory Outputs in End-to-End Autonomous Driving via SC-IMM Based Teacher Signals
papers.title_zh: Stabilizing Trajectory Outputs in End-to-End Autonomous Driving via SC-IMM Based Teacher Signals
papers.tldr_zh: End-to-End autonomous driving models commonly predict future
papers.cover_zh: End-to-End autonomous driving models commonly predict future
papers.abstract_zh: End-to-End autonomous driving models commonly predict future waypoints from sensor inputs and convert them into vehicle control commands through a downstream controller. However, conventional waypoint-based imitation learning mainly minimizes coordinate-level errors, making it difficult to capture scene-dependent path-speed changes and temporal instability across waypoint outputs. In this paper, we propose an offline teacher-signal generation and learning method for trajectory-output stabilization based on a Scene-Conditioned Interacting Multiple Model (SC-IMM) to mitigate this issue. The proposed method converts expert trajectories into path-speed states and performs IMM updates conditioned on scene cues to generate path-speed teacher labels and mode posterior probabilities. The generated signals are added to the original trajectory loss as auxiliary supervision during training, while the inference structure and waypoint controller remain unchanged. In closed-loop evaluation on 100 short routes in CARLA Town12, the proposed method improved the driving score by 28.0% and reduced Collision/km by 62.3% compared with the baseline, while also improving jerk and trajectory-variation metrics. These results demonstrate that offline teacher signals embedding scene-conditioned motion-model cues can guide trajectory-output driving models toward more stable closed-loop behavior.

papers.title: SkillIR: Evolving Scene-Aware Skills for Agentic Image Restoration
papers.title_zh: SkillIR: Evolving Scene-Aware Skills for Agentic Image Restoration
papers.tldr_zh: This paper studies agentic image restoration, in which multi
papers.cover_zh: This paper studies agentic image restoration, in which multi
papers.abstract_zh: This paper studies agentic image restoration, in which multimodal agents coordinate specialized restoration tools to recover images affected by complex degradations. Existing restoration agents often derive complete tool-use plans from the original degraded image or retrieve previously successful trajectories, providing limited support for adapting individual actions to evolving intermediate restoration states. We find that accepted tool executions can change the residual degradation state and, consequently, the applicability of subsequent tools. To address this issue, we propose SkillIR, a skill-guided framework that represents restoration experience as degradation-centered action evidence rather than complete tool-use trajectories. SkillIR consolidates context-dependent action outcomes into scene-aware restoration skills that characterize applicable conditions, expected effects, and attributable failure cases. Instead of prescribing a complete restoration plan, the retrieved skills guide one bounded action at a time within a verified residual-state loop: each tool output is treated as a candidate, committed only after transition verification, and followed by reassessment of the active residual degradations. After each rollout, the resulting evidence is used to create, refine, or patch dynamic skills, enabling accumulated restoration experience to improve decision-making for subsequent inputs. Experiments on synthetic and real-world multi-degradation datasets demonstrate that SkillIR improves restoration quality and enables more reliable and effective tool use.

papers.title: Tilt as a Certified Resource: Preserving Motor Wrench-Rate Authority on Articulated Multirotors
papers.title_zh: Tilt as a Certified Resource: Preserving Motor Wrench-Rate Authority on Articulated Multirotors
papers.tldr_zh: Fully-actuated multirotor aerial vehicles must not only trac
papers.cover_zh: Fully-actuated multirotor aerial vehicles must not only trac
papers.abstract_zh: Fully-actuated multirotor aerial vehicles must not only track nominal wrenches but retain the "readiness" to modulate them rapidly under disturbances. Classical effort-minimizing allocators ignore this dynamic limit, whereas maximizing readiness leads to topologically disconnected optimal sheets demanding physically impossible actuator rates. Enforcing a readiness safety floor on fixed-geometry symmetric platforms further encounters a zero-sum degeneracy: motor-speed redistribution cannot improve authority without conceding wrench tracking. This paper uses active morphology to break the degeneracy, treating servo tilt as a geometric resource supplying authority-recovery directions unavailable to static rotors. We construct a configuration-dependent, motor-only readiness certificate - the log-volume of the reachable wrench-rate set - that explicitly excludes servo capacity, preventing a "ghost capacity fallacy" in which the certificate would falsely credit slow mechanical kinematic limits instead of collapsing accurately at motor saturation. The certificate is enforced as a Control Barrier Function (CBF) within a Unified Physical-Command Quadratic Program acting on motor torques and servo setpoints. Closed-loop simulations of an articulated octorotor under severe gust disturbances show classical allocators diverging and uncertified articulated allocators violating the safety floor, while the proposed CBF filter bounds the system state and preserves vehicle authority.

papers.title: A High-Payload Wall-Climbing Robot Using Passive Bistable Suction Cups
papers.title_zh: A High-Payload Wall-Climbing Robot Using Passive Bistable Suction Cups
papers.tldr_zh: Wall-climbing robots capable of scaling vertical surfaces co
papers.cover_zh: Wall-climbing robots capable of scaling vertical surfaces co
papers.abstract_zh: Wall-climbing robots capable of scaling vertical surfaces could help automate hazardous or labor intensive tasks such as window washing, inspection, maintenance, and construction. Active adhesion methods achieve higher payload capacities, but require power to maintain their grip. Passive adhesion devices such as suction cups are an attractive option for such robots because they do not require power to maintain their grip, but they are limited by their payload capacity. This work presents a novel high-payload wall-climbing robot that utilizes passive bistable suction cups to generate adhesion without needing to be pushed into the wall. The robot features a track-based system that automatically engages and disengages bistable suction cups to achieve locomotion on smooth surfaces. The robot is able to achieve vertical wall climbing on glass, wood, metal, and painted surfaces, sideways and upside-down climbing, and is able to tow a payload of 7.940 kg (with a payload-to-weight ratio of 2.25).

papers.title: Detection is solved, delineation is not: what governs tooth segmentation on panoramic radiographs
papers.title_zh: Detection is solved, delineation is not: what governs tooth segmentation on panoramic radiographs
papers.tldr_zh: Automatic tooth segmentation and FDI numbering on panoramic
papers.cover_zh: Automatic tooth segmentation and FDI numbering on panoramic
papers.abstract_zh: Automatic tooth segmentation and FDI numbering on panoramic radiographs underpins computer-assisted dental diagnosis, yet which factors govern performance remains unclear. We assemble a corpus of 1,422 panoramic radiographs containing 42,142 expert-delineated tooth polygons across the 32-class FDI taxonomy, annotated by 30 dental practitioners and independently reviewed by two others, and use it to isolate input resolution, architecture and anatomical priors under a single evaluation protocol. First, resolution dominates: across a controlled 640/1024/1280 ablation, mask mAP50-95 rises 0.656 -> 0.710 -> 0.717 while mAP50 stays flat at ~0.982. Both gains are significant under a paired bootstrap over images (p < 0.001, p = 0.024); neither mAP50 change is distinguishable from zero. Added resolution buys boundary precision, not detection. Second, architecture is nearly irrelevant in-domain: a query-based transformer with 2.1x the parameters is statistically equivalent to a one-stage detector (95% CI [-0.0064, +0.0064]), only marginally better under domain shift, 5.5x slower on CPU and not executable under standard ONNX runtimes. Third, three targeted interventions fail: a LoRA-adapted self-supervised encoder underperforms, a promptable foundation segmenter degrades masks by 39%, and globally optimal anatomical label assignment yields +0.0007 despite correcting a constraint violated in 40% of out-of-domain predictions. Zero-shot transfer to an independent multi-centre cohort, verified overlap-free, costs 62% of mask mAP50-95 but only 18% of mAP50, reproducing the dissociation. Decomposing masks along the tooth axis localises the residual error to the apical third. Boundary precision is therefore the binding constraint, and effort is better directed at resolution and acquisition diversity than at architectural novelty.

papers.title: Bayesian classification of astronomical spectra with class uncertainties
papers.title_zh: Bayesian classification of astronomical spectra with class uncertainties
papers.tldr_zh: Context: We developed a probabilistic machine learning metho
papers.cover_zh: Context: We developed a probabilistic machine learning metho
papers.abstract_zh: Context: We developed a probabilistic machine learning method with the aim of performing the O(10)-way classification of low- and high-resolution spectra of stellar and extragalactic targets for the upcoming 4MOST survey. In fulfilment of the survey requirements, this method should be able to express uncertainty in the input data as well as uncertainty introduced in its prediction. Aims: Four different methods are explored: (1) convolutional neural networks (CNNs), (2) the Dirichlet distribution, (3) Monte Carlo dropout (MCD), (4) Bayesian neural Networks (BNNs) + variational inference (VI). Training and validation was performed using labelled spectra from the SDSS database and a custom 4MOST mock dataset. All the methods were compared in terms of the same metrics: accuracy, area under the curve (AUC), expected calibration error (ECE), Shannon entropy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), Brier score, training time, and inference time. Methods: A CNN with simple architecture and about 20,000 parameters was trained to achieve classification accuracies of 91.5% on SDSS data and 92.8% on 4MOST mock data. The direct Dirichlet prediction and VI models tested provide uncertainties on class membership probabilities, but they confuse classes more often. The MCD on a CNN is found to be the most suitable; it boosts the point-estimate accuracies to 92.6% and 93.9%, while still providing fast training and sufficiently fast inference. Compared to a standard CNN, the method additionally provides well-calibrated uncertainties at marginal extra cost.

papers.title: TRACE: Coverage Path Planning for Unknown Environments Using Hierarchical Coverage Tree
papers.title_zh: TRACE：使用分层覆盖树在未知环境中进行覆盖路径规划
papers.tldr_zh: TRACE算法利用分层覆盖树实现未知环境的高效在线覆盖路径规划。
papers.cover_zh: 未知环境全覆盖还能这么丝滑？TRACE用分层树让路径规划不再反复重算
papers.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种新颖的在线覆盖路径规划（CPP）算法，称为TRACE，用于未知环境的实时覆盖。TRACE基于分层覆盖树构建，该树提供了未覆盖空间不断变化的连通性的全局表示。随着环境被逐步揭示和覆盖，新发现的障碍物和已覆盖的单元格可能将剩余的未覆盖空间分割成不连通的区域。TRACE递归地扩展相应的树节点以显式表示这些区域，并组织它们以进行后续的覆盖规划。基于更新后的树，维护一个增量全局巡回以指导覆盖过程。TRACE仅局部细化受影响的部分，同时保持未变化区域的访问顺序，从而减少了全局重新规划的计算负担，并保持了覆盖进程的一致性。在全局巡回的指导下，局部规划器生成来回覆盖路径，并切换到全局巡回感知规划以高效完成目标区域。理论分析建立了TRACE的计算复杂度和完全覆盖性质，并推导了增量全局巡回细化的近似界。通过使用移动机器人进行的大量高保真仿真和真实机器人实验，评估了TRACE的性能。与六种现有CPP方法的比较评估表明，在覆盖时间、路径长度、重叠率和转弯次数方面均有显著改进。

papers.title: Gripper-Aware Automatic Dense Packing of Irregular Objects
papers.title_zh: 夹爪感知的不规则物体自动密集装箱
papers.tldr_zh: 提出闭环流水线，集成夹爪感知优化与力引导执行，实现真实机器人不规则物体密集装箱。
papers.cover_zh: 夹爪也能参与规划？｜这个闭环系统让不规则物体装箱更密集
papers.abstract_zh: 自动密集装箱在仓储作业中广受期待，但在机器人操作中仍是一个基础性挑战。现有的不规则物体装箱工作大多针对理想接触的仿真，将物体视为孤立的刚体。夹爪通常仅作为离散的事后可行性检查，甚至完全不予考虑，且执行过程中累积的感知和接触漂移也未得到处理。我们提出了一种闭环流水线，在真实机械臂上集成了感知、夹爪感知的放置优化和力引导执行。优化器将物体与夹爪表示为分层球树构成的单一复合体。它在GPU上以CMA-ES框架搜索五个自由度，垂直坐标基于当前高度图解析确定。在执行过程中，力监控的垂直下降在首次接触时停止。释放后的整合推动则消除夹爪感知规划留下的残余横向间隙。每次放置之间重新感知容器，以避免漂移累积。我们在Franka Emika Panda机器人上验证了系统，装箱了3D打印的平面、曲面和凹面物体集合以及YCB物体子集。消融研究分离了夹爪感知优化、整合推动和网格导出几何对端到端成功率、达到的密度和计算成本的贡献。我们进一步以高度图最小化方法作为先前不规则物体装箱工作的基线代表进行了基准测试。

papers.title: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
papers.title_zh: MintAct：面向数字环境的统一视觉智能体
papers.tldr_zh: MintAct 统一视觉智能体，跨域性能媲美专用模型。
papers.cover_zh: 一个模型通吃手机桌面网页｜MintAct 让专用模型慌了
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出了 MintAct，一个视觉语言模型系列，统一了 UI 定位、跨移动端、桌面端和网页的多步导航以及视觉工具使用，并在 2B、4B 和 8B 规模上进行了训练。通过精心设计环境、数据和训练方案，MintAct 模型在所有上述能力上均达到了各领域专用模型的性能水平。为实现这一目标，我们开发了可扩展的环境和强化学习（RL）基础设施。在环境方面，我们托管了数百个跨异构领域后端的并发实例，同时服务于轨迹数据收集和在线 RL。为了实现高效且可扩展的 RL 训练，异步框架对跨领域训练分布保持显式控制，并在噪声环境反馈和离策略漂移下保持稳定。实验结果表明，MintAct 在同等模型规模下，在广泛的基准测试中达到了最先进的性能（OSWorld-Verified 上为 48.9）。
